To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we give a distributed algorithm to compute routing tables in time ~O(ε-1/2+log ε-1+HD) for any constant ε > 0, and (2) we give an algorithm to compute routing table entries with high probability in time ~O(HD) for any constant c ≥ 2.

(a) the Omega(n) barrier for computing routing tables and approximate shortest distances in a distributed manner can be broken; (b) the Omega(n1/2) complexity of computing routing tables in a distributed manner is nearly optimal; and (c) the algorithm is simple, and can be implemented with a very small number of messages.

(1) the diameter of a network (in hops, as if it is unweighted) is a good measure of its complexity for distributed algorithms, and (2) the diameter of the weighted network (as if it is unweighed) is also a good measure of complexity for the distributed computation of routing table.
